title: A Special Saturday
topic: 日常生活・野餐・天氣
text:
On Saturday morning I woke up early. The [[sun]] was bright and the sky was clear, so I knew it would be a fine day. My mother was already in the [[kitchen]]. She was making breakfast, and the smell of fresh [[bread]] filled the house.

"Do you remember your plan?" she asked. "You will meet your friends at nine."

I had forgotten! Our class had a [[picnic]] at the park near the river. I put on a clean T-shirt and my favorite blue [[jacket]], and then I packed my bag. My mother gave me a big bottle of water and some cookies. "Do not lose your key," she said.

I rode my [[bicycle]] to the park. It took me twenty minutes. My classmates were already there. Some of them were playing basketball. Some were sitting on the [[grass]] under a big tree. Our teacher brought a Frisbee, and we played with it for an hour. I was so [[tired]] that I had to rest on a bench.

At [[noon]] we shared our food. There were sandwiches, rice, fruit, and a large cake. All of it tasted [[delicious]]. My friend Amy told a story about her little brother, and we all began to [[laugh]].

In the afternoon the sky became dark and the [[wind]] grew strong. "It may rain soon," our teacher said. "We should go home now." Ten minutes later the rain fell. We ran to the bus stop and waited there, wet but glad.

That night, before I went to sleep, I wrote about the day in my [[notebook]]. The weather was terrible at the end, but it was still one of the great days of the year.

title: My Family's Restaurant
text:
My parents own a small [[restaurant]] near the train station. It is not big, but it is always busy. My father is the [[cook]]. He gets up at five every morning to buy fresh [[vegetable]]s and meat at the market. My mother is the [[boss]]. She takes the orders, talks to the guests, and counts the money at the end of the day.

On Saturdays I help them. I wear a clean white [[shirt]] and carry the plates to the tables. It is not easy work. Once I dropped a [[bowl]] of hot soup on the floor and everyone looked at me. My face turned [[red]]. My mother only smiled and said, "Do not worry. Try again."

Our [[menu]] is short. We sell beef noodles, dumplings, fried rice, and three kinds of soup. The beef noodle soup is the most [[popular]] dish. Many people come from other towns just to [[taste]] it. My father will not tell anyone how he makes it, not even me.

The busiest time is between six and eight in the [[evening]]. Sometimes there is no seat left, and people must wait outside on the sidewalk. My mother gives them hot [[tea]] while they wait.

At nine o'clock we close the door. My father cooks one last [[meal]] for our family. We sit at the table together and eat. He is always tired, but he looks glad.

"Do you want to be a cook someday?" he asked me last week.

I am not sure. Being a cook is [[difficult]] work. But when I watch my father cook, I think it is also a kind of art.

title: The Trip to the Island
text:
Last summer my class took a [[trip]] to a small island in the south. We left the school at six in the morning and rode a [[bus]] to the harbor. Then we got on a [[ship]]. The way across the water took two hours.

I had never been on a boat before. At first the [[sea]] was calm and the sky was clear. I stood outside and watched the birds. Later the wind grew stronger and the boat began to [[move]] up and down. My [[stomach]] felt terrible. My classmate Ben gave me some [[medicine]] and told me to look at the mountain far away. It helped.

When we arrived, the island was quieter than I expected. There were no high buildings, only small houses with white [[wall]]s. An old [[fisherman]] was fixing his net beside the water. He smiled at us and said hello.

We walked along the [[beach]] and collected shells. The sand was warm under our feet. Our teacher showed us a [[map]] and explained how the island was made long ago. Then we ate lunch under a big tree. Nothing tasted better than cold [[watermelon]] on a hot day.

In the afternoon we climbed a small [[hill]]. From the top we could see the whole island and the blue sea around it. Some students took [[photo]]s. I just stood there and looked.

On the way home everyone was quiet. Most of my classmates fell asleep on the boat. I stayed awake and watched the sun go down. The sky turned orange, then purple, then dark.

It was a long day, but I would go again tomorrow.
